an1.576-582:1.1: _Yogakkhema_ (“sanctuary from the yoke”) is a metaphor for Nibbana that draws from the literal sense of _khema_ as an oasis or sanctuary for men and beasts. After a hard day’s journey, a caravan would stop to rest, “unyoke” the draft animals, lay down the burden, and refresh themselves in the cool waters.
an1.586-590:1.1: From here to the end of the Ones, the texts are presented in the Mahāsaṅgīti edition as concatenated ranges. That is, they appear to be a series of separate suttas, but the set of main terms appears at both the beginning and the end of the series. For this reason the range as it stands cannot be resolved to its individual members. This varies per edition. In BJT each sutta appears in full, whereas in PTS the texts do not repeat the main terms at the end. The commentary does not decide this matter.
an1.591-592:1.1: For _pabhedāya_, see _avijjāya pabhedanaṁ_, the “smashing of ignorance” ([an3.33:4.2]() = [snp5.14:2.3](); also [an4.178:3.2]()). The commentaries, however, take it in the sense of “differentiation”.
an1.593-595:1.1: In early texts, _paṭisambhidā_ is found only in the Aṅguttara, and elsewhere only in the group of four kinds of textual analysis. The commentary explains it here as the knowledge of classifying elements by way of predominant cause.
